name: Content Signals
description: Checks whether the site declares Content Signals (search, ai-input, ai-train = yes/no) in robots.txt or in a Content-Signal response header. robots.txt only says whether a crawler may fetch; Content Signals state what AI companies may do with the content (index it, ground answers on it, train on it).
inputs: HTTP response headers of the page (plain GET)
HTTP response headers of the page requested with Accept: text/markdown, text/html;q=0.9
AI bot list: keys of src/data/robots.json (ai-robots-txt project)

scoring.summary: Parse Content-Signal lines in robots.txt (served root) and a Content-Signal header from host config for '/' (_headers, vercel.json, netlify.toml). At least one valid key=yes|no pair in either -> 3 (predicted when it comes only from the header). Else, if robots.txt is generated and cannot be read -> 2 inconclusive. Else if robots.txt has a User-agent line naming any AI bot -> 1. Else 0.

rules.condition: Content-Signal directives from lib/robots.mjs parseRobots (anywhere in the file, independent of User-agent groups; '#' comments stripped). Later lines override earlier keys.
split on ','; each part split on '='; key trimmed/lowercased must be one of [search, ai-input, ai-train]; value trimmed/lowercased must be exactly 'yes' or 'no'. Other pairs ignored.
content-signal from site.host.headersFor('/') (first rule with a valid pair). Parsed with the same value parser.
combined = {...headerSignals, ...robotsSignals} (robots wins on conflicts). source = both | robots | header.
at least one valid signal parsed from robots.txt or header
rules.note: predicted: true when the only source is host header config

rules.condition: no valid signals, no robots.txt file, and Generated robots.txt (no file in the served root, but src/pages/robots.txt.*, app/robots.*, robots.njk/robots.11ty.js, Hugo enableRobotsTXT, astro-robots-txt / next-sitemap, or a CMS in report-only mode)
no valid signals, and a robots.txt User-agent token (lowercased, comments stripped) equals a name in references/ai-bots.json (case-insensitive)

scoring.status_mapping: Derived by the engine from the integer score: >= 80% pass, >= 50% warning, else fail; inconclusive results are always a warning.
scoring.inconclusive: Only when robots.txt is generated and not in the served root and no header signal is configured: 2/3, inconclusive true (the extension's value for its all-unreachable branch).

detect.source_procedure: 1) Read robots.txt from the served root and extract Content-Signal lines with lib/robots.mjs. 2) Read a Content-Signal header for '/' from _headers, vercel.json headers or netlify.toml [[headers]] (site.host.headersFor). 3) Any valid pair -> 3. 4) Else a generated robots.txt -> 2 inconclusive. 5) Else User-agent lines naming an AI bot -> 1. 6) Else 0.
detect.llm_criteria: Only for generated robots.txt or header code paths (template logic, env-dependent output): decide what literal robots.txt text and response headers production would emit, then apply the rules mechanically.

parity.note: Hosts and CDNs can add robots.txt content or the Content-Signal header outside the repo (notably Cloudflare managed robots.txt, which injects Content-Signal lines, and Cloudflare Markdown for Agents which sets the header on markdown responses). Generated robots.txt may depend on env vars. The unreachable branch cannot be reproduced from source.

fix_summary: Add a line such as 'Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=no' to robots.txt (public/robots.txt for Astro/Next/Vite, static/robots.txt for Hugo, root or passthrough for static/Eleventy, or the generator for app/robots.ts and Hugo robots templates). The yes/no values are a policy choice, so the plugin should propose defaults and let the user confirm; optionally also add a Content-Signal header via _headers, netlify.toml or vercel.json.

divergences.extension: Signals come from live robots.txt, the page response header and the Accept: text/markdown response header; all three unreachable -> 2 inconclusive.
divergences.plugin: robots.txt from the served root and the header from host config for '/'; the Markdown response header (set by CDNs such as Cloudflare) cannot be seen. A generated robots.txt is the inconclusive (2) case; a header-only pass is marked predicted.

divergences.extension: A Content-Signal value with a trailing '# comment' is invalid, and 'User-agent: GPTBot # note' does not count as addressing the bot.
divergences.reason: robots.txt comment syntax; the extension missed valid declarations.

divergences.extension: If robots.txt alone is unreachable but the page responded without a header, the check fails with 0.
divergences.plugin: No equivalent: a robots.txt that exists in the repo is always read; only a generated one is inconclusive.

divergences.extension: Reads Content-Signal from the fetched robots.txt and the page response header.
divergences.plugin: URL mode: reads Content-Signal lines from the fetched robots.txt and the real Content-Signal response header of every audited page (first valid one wins, measured, not predicted). When robots.txt is unreachable (0, 401, 403, 429, 503, timeout) and no page sends the header the result is inconclusive at 2/3, not 0. A 404 robots.txt is absent. Generator logic is skipped.
divergences.reason: Unreachable-vs-absent rule in the project CLAUDE.md; URL mode measures instead of predicting.
